newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end volatile week on weak note.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end volatile week on weak note.

text.p: Concerns over slower profits and growth from lending curbs overcame a mild recovery in Kuala Lumpur shares earlier this week, leading the market to end on a down note on Friday.
The Composite Index of blue chips sank over two percent in intraday business on Friday before clipping the losses to 0.84 percent, off 9.60 points to 1,138.36.

While new restrictions by Bank Negara on property and stock loans may be positive for the market in the long-term, "in the short-term, people say they won't buy (stocks) because there's no performance," said an analyst with a foreign research firm.
On Tuesday, the blue chip barometer recouped 2.47 percent. The Composite Index edged up just 1.60 points on Wednesday.
"Prices look good but people don't think it's time to buy yet," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.
He said that stocks like Telekom and United Engineers were at attractive valuations.
One analyst said investors are holding back until banks report to Bank Negara on how they will comply with the new lending restrictions.
